Cyber Attack Hits Uzbekistan Engineering and Construction Firms, Disrupting Operations

A major cyber attack has struck several firms in Uzbekistan’s engineering and construction sector, resulting in widespread disruptions to project management systems and IT infrastructure. Among the companies affected is China Petroleum Engineering Corp, one of the largest players in the country’s booming energy construction market.

The incident, understood to have begun on Monday morning, appears to be a coordinated ransomware attack targeting the firms’ internal networks. According to the Uzbekistan Association of Construction and Engineering Enterprises, at least five major companies have reported system outages, with engineers and project managers unable to access critical design files and procurement databases.

“Operational paralysis is the best way to describe it,” said Shavkat Ergashev, spokesperson for the association. “With core systems offline, everything from planning to supply chain coordination is at a standstill for many of our members.” At the time of writing, restoration efforts were ongoing, with IT teams working around the clock to contain the breach and retrieve encrypted data.

China Petroleum Engineering Corp confirmed in a statement that its Tashkent office was experiencing “significant technical difficulties” due to the attack, which has forced the company to temporarily suspend several ongoing projects. “Our immediate priority is to protect our project data and resume operations as swiftly as possible,” a company spokesperson said, declining to comment on whether ransom demands had been received.

Industry analysts estimate that the attack could delay key infrastructure projects by at least one to two weeks if not resolved promptly. “The timing is especially damaging as many firms are entering the peak season for construction,” said Uzbek business analyst Dilshod Rakhimov. He warned that extended disruptions could lead to financial penalties and increased costs for contractors.

The Ministry of Digital Technologies has urged all engineering and construction firms to review their cybersecurity protocols and report any suspicious activity. “This incident highlights the growing threat of cyber crime in our rapidly modernizing sector,” said Deputy Minister Feruza Akbarova. “We are coordinating efforts to support affected companies and restore critical services.”

As of Tuesday afternoon, the attack remained ongoing and no timeline for full recovery had been announced.
